S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

info.persona: Courtney Aldrich is a 19‑year‑old tech‑savvy visual storyteller who channels curiosity into data art, thrives on spontaneous bursts of creation, battles deadline‑avoidance, and balances a love for indie music, cryptic puzzles, and occasional caffeine‑induced overwork.
info.professional_persona: An emerging data visualization specialist and freelance UX designer, Courtney Aldrich leverages Python, C++, Blender, and Adobe Illustrator to craft interactive scientific dashboards, yet their spontaneous, deadline‑averse streak often leads to late‑night bursts of creativity rather than structured project timelines.
info.cultural_background: Courtney grew up in Leechburg, a modest industrial town in Armstrong County, Pennsylvania. Her family traces its roots to German and Irish immigrants who settled in the region during the early 20th century, instilling a strong work ethic and a sense of self‑reliance. The town’s blue‑collar heritage and close‑knit community shaped her values of independence and practicality, while the local art scene—small galleries, community theater, and annual river festivals—nurtured her appreciation for creativity. Being raised in a predominantly white Midwestern environment, she experienced traditional modesty but also leveraged online platforms to absorb global cultural influences, allowing her to balance respect for her hometown’s heritage with an open, unconventional worldview.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Courtney immerses herself in both artistic and intellectual pursuits. She sketches and creates digital illustrations, often experimenting with mixed media. Photography is a favorite outlet, especially capturing the industrial decay and natural scenery around the Allegheny River. She devours science‑fiction novels and follows podcasts that explore cutting‑edge science and art. Her hands‑on curiosity leads her to tinker with Arduino and Raspberry Pi projects, build custom mechanical keyboards, and explore virtual‑reality art installations. Competitive activities keep her engaged: she plays chess, participates in online coding hackathons, and enjoys small‑group board‑game evenings with close friends. Nature hikes and coffee‑shop journaling round out her solitary yet adventurous weekends.
info.sports_persona: An outdoor‑leaning hobbyist, Courtney Aldrich spends weekends hiking the Allegheny River trails and occasional rock‑climbing at a local gym, follows the Pittsburgh Steelers, Penguins, and Pirates faithfully, and occasionally participates in a local ultimate frisbee pick‑up group during summer.
info.arts_persona: An interdisciplinary creator, Courtney Aldrich blends digital illustration with experimental music, drawing inspiration from artists like Beeple and musicians such as Tycho and Ólafur Arnalds, and regularly attends the annual Pittsburgh Arts Festival to showcase her mixed‑media sketches.
info.travel_persona: A curiosity‑driven wanderer, Courtney Aldrich maps out spontaneous weekend getaways to nearby destinations like the Laurel Highlands and occasionally plans longer trips to Kyoto to explore the blend of traditional temples and cutting‑edge tech culture, preferring budget‑friendly hostels over luxury hotels while balancing student finances.
info.culinary_persona: A recipe‑tinkering food lover, Courtney Aldrich enjoys cooking matcha‑infused ramen, mastering the perfect cauliflower crust pizza, and experimenting with smoked paprika‑seasoned lentil tacos, but often forgets to meal‑prep, leading to late‑night fast‑food orders after coding marathons.

info.persona: Baha Ogura, a disciplined 37‑year‑old firefighter who blends curiosity for technology with hands‑on creativity, they turn every emergency, hike, and kitchen experiment into a chance to learn, lead, and improve, and they never shy away from a new challenge.
info.professional_persona: Baha Ogura, a seasoned firefighter with an associate degree in Fire Science, leverages strong expertise in fire suppression, hazardous‑materials response, and incident command while integrating emerging technologies like drone aerial reconnaissance and predictive fire modeling, and they pursue a path toward captaincy, battalion chief leadership, and eventually a training officer role.
info.cultural_background: Baha grew up in a middle‑class suburban family on Long Island, with deep roots in the Northeastern United States and a mixed European heritage that includes Irish and Italian ancestry. Though his surname reflects a Japanese lineage, his cultural upbringing has been predominantly American, shaped by the diverse environment of Queens and the greater New York area. He values community service, a principle reinforced by his family's tradition of volunteerism, and he celebrates mainstream American holidays while also participating in the multicultural festivals that define his neighborhood. This blend of heritage and local diversity informs his respectful, inclusive outlook and his commitment to public safety.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Baha maintains a disciplined fitness routine that includes strength training, running, and occasional basketball games with friends. He enjoys exploring the outdoors through hiking trips to nearby state parks and weekend camping excursions. His curiosity extends to photography, where he captures urban landscapes and nature scenes, and to woodworking, a hobby that satisfies his practical creativity. Baha also likes cooking, experimenting with new recipes, and listening to podcasts on science, technology, and history. He participates in local fire safety workshops as a volunteer educator and takes part in community events that celebrate the cultural diversity of Queens.
info.sports_persona: Baha Ogura stays active with strength training, weekly runs that qualify them for the Queens Half‑Marathon, and pickup basketball games with the local YMCA league, while cheering on the New York Knicks and New York Yankees, and they maintain a membership in the Queens Running Club.
info.arts_persona: Baha Ogura expresses creative energy through photography inspired by Ansel Adams and Steve McCurry, woodworking projects echoing the style of Sam Maloof, and a playlist that mixes John Coltrane with The Black Keys, and they use every free moment to capture urban skylines or craft functional art for their firehouse crew.
info.travel_persona: Baha Ogura prefers weekend escapes to state parks like the Adirondacks and Shenandoah for hiking and camping, while also planning annual trips to tech‑savvy cities like Tokyo and historic sites in Rome, and they balance meticulous route planning with spontaneous detours to capture drone footage of remote vistas.
info.culinary_persona: Baha Ogura, an enthusiastic home cook, experiments with dishes such as spicy Korean bibimbap, miso‑glazed salmon, and wood‑fired pizza, favoring ingredients like smoked paprika, saffron, and fresh herbs, and they regularly host post‑shift potlucks where colleagues sample their latest culinary creations.

info.persona: Miriam Valencia is a methodical environmental consultant who balances meticulous budgeting, a love for volcanic hikes, and a quirky habit of humming salsa while planting coffee seedlings in their backyard garden.
info.professional_persona: Miriam Valencia, a remote environmental consultant with a solid background in environmental science, uses GIS, R, and Python to deliver data‑driven sustainability plans for small farms, while their structured, practical mindset ensures projects stay on schedule and budgets are meticulously managed.
info.cultural_background: Miriam’s cultural identity is rooted in her Puerto Rican heritage, a blend of Afro‑Caribbean and Spanish traditions that emphasize family, music, and food. Raised bilingual in Spanish and English, she carries forward the island’s vibrant customs—salsa, bomba, and festive gatherings centered around dishes like lechón and arroz con gandules. Her Catholic upbringing instilled a sense of community service and resilience. Since moving to Pahala, Hawaii, Miriam has embraced the local Hawaiian respect for ‘āina (the land) and the spirit of aloha, integrating these values into her daily life. She participates in island cultural events, learns Hawaiian language basics, and honors the island’s natural beauty through sustainable gardening. This dual cultural lens informs her worldview, shaping her compassionate yet pragmatic approach to family, work, and community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Miriam’s hobbies reflect her love for structure, nature, and cultural expression. She maintains an organized organic garden where she cultivates coffee, papaya, and native Hawaiian plants, following seasonal planting schedules. Cooking is a creative outlet; she enjoys perfecting traditional Puerto Rican dishes such as mofongo and arroz con gandules, often incorporating locally sourced fish and fruit. On weekends, she hikes the trails around Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, capturing photos of volcanic landscapes and native birds. Miriam volunteers with local environmental clean‑up teams and leads educational walks for visitors. Music also plays a role in her life—she plays the ukulele and practices salsa rhythms, and she attends community festivals that celebrate both Hawaiian and Puerto Rican cultures. Reading science fiction and popular science keeps her curiosity sharp, while occasional DIY home improvement projects satisfy her practical side.
info.sports_persona: Miriam Valencia hikes the volcanic trails of Hawaii Volcanoes National Park most weekends, joins a local adult volleyball league with the Honolulu Hurricanes, and follows the University of Hawaii Rainbow Warriors basketball team, balancing outdoor cardio with community team spirit.
info.arts_persona: Miriam Valencia plays the ukulele to the soothing tunes of Jake Shimabukuro and practices salsa rhythms inspired by Marc Anthony, attends cultural festivals featuring hula and Caribbean dance performances, and reads science‑fiction works by N.K. Jemisin and popular science by Carl Sagan.
info.travel_persona: Miriam Valencia prefers well‑planned eco‑tourism trips, having explored the rainforests of Costa Rica, the historic streets of Old San Juan, and the geothermal wonders of Iceland, while they dream of a sustainable homestay in the Azores to study volcanic soils.
info.culinary_persona: Miriam Valencia blends Caribbean flavors with Hawaiian ingredients, perfecting dishes like mofongo with macadamia‑crusted fish and serving aromatic coffee blends infused with papaya zest, often sourcing fresh catch from local fish markets and using organic lime and cilantro.
